title: Your colleague went to the fair
hook: Could an invitation affect people who never received it?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Identify spillovers to colleagues and distinguish them from direct treatment effects.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Identify spillovers to colleagues and distinguish them from direct treatment effects.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: Toy enrollment is 60% for directly invited staff, 50% for uninvited peers, and 40% in control. What is the peer-versus-control difference? Toy inputs A=[60, 50, 40]; B=[60, 40, 40].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[20, 10, 40], [20, 0, 40]]. Labels: Direct lift pp, Peer lift pp, Control %.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Direct treatment and exposure through colleagues are separate comparisons. The second case has no peer difference despite the same direct difference. A study design needs to account for such spillovers rather than treating all uninvited people as unexposed.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Direct %=60, Peer %=40, Control %=40. What is Peer lift pp? Answer: 0.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Direct %=60, Peer %=40, Control %=40. What is Peer lift pp?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Inviting university staff to a benefits fair, with a small payment, raised retirement plan enrollment, also among their colleagues (Duflo & Saez, 2003).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Identify spillovers to colleagues and distinguish them from direct treatment effects.
